target.title: fix(slack): omit reply_to_id for non-reply inbound messages (#102457)
target.body:
## Summary

In the Slack channel plugin, `resolveSlackThreadContext` computed `replyToId` as `incomingThreadTs ?? messageTs` without checking the `isThreadReply` flag it derives one line above. As a result, the `reply_to_id` field of the inbound "Conversation info" prompt metadata equaled `message_id` for every inbound message that is not a genuine thread reply.

Fixes #102457.

## What Problem This Solves

`reply_to_id` should identify the message a reply is responding to, and be omitted when the message is not a reply. Before this fix it was wrong for the majority of Slack traffic:

- **Standalone message** (no `thread_ts`): `replyToId` fell through the `??` to `messageTs`, so it equaled `message_id`.
- **Thread-root message** (`thread_ts == ts`, including the Slack Agents/Assistants DM root case): `replyToId` became `incomingThreadTs`, which equals `messageTs`, so it again equaled `message_id`.
- Only a **genuine reply** (`thread_ts` present and different from `ts`) was correct.

That corrupts a semantic signal in the untrusted prompt metadata that both the model and internal logic read — e.g. `chatWindowCoversReplyContext` in `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts` branches on `replyToId` truthiness to decide reply-chain coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSlackThreadContext` already derives `isThreadReply`, and its sibling `resolveSlackThreadTargets` in the same file already gates on it correctly for outbound threading. The inbound `replyToId` formula simply never applied the same gate. Gating it is narrowly scoped: `threadContext.replyToId` is consumed at exactly one call site (the inbound prompt metadata field), so the fix does not touch outbound reply threading, session routing, or thread-id derivation, which use separate fields (`messageThreadId`, `incomingThreadTs`, `isThreadReply`).

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/threading.ts`: `replyToId = isThreadReply ? incomingThreadTs : undefined` (was `incomingThreadTs ?? messageTs`).
- `extensions/slack/src/threading.test.ts`: added focused `replyToId` gating tests and corrected existing assertions that had frozen the buggy `replyToId == message_id` value for non-reply messages.

## User Impact

Every Slack integration: non-reply inbound messages (the majority of traffic) now get `reply_to_id` omitted instead of falsely equal to `message_id`. Genuine threaded replies are unaffected — they still carry the parent message's timestamp.

## Evidence

### 1. Real setup transcript (standalone, not a test harness)

A standalone script drove the real `resolveSlackThreadContext` with the three inbound shapes, run against `origin/main` and against this patch on identical inputs:

```
# BEFORE (origin/main — replyToId = incomingThreadTs ?? messageTs)
standalone (no thread_ts)     | message_id=1751234567.123456 isThreadReply=false reply_to_id="1751234567.123456"
thread-root (thread_ts==ts)   | message_id=1751234567.123456 isThreadReply=false reply_to_id="1751234567.123456"
genuine reply (thread_ts!=ts) | message_id=1751234599.999999 isThreadReply=true reply_to_id="1751234567.123456"

# AFTER (this PR — replyToId = isThreadReply ? incomingThreadTs : undefined)
standalone (no thread_ts)     | message_id=1751234567.123456 isThreadReply=false reply_to_id=undefined
thread-root (thread_ts==ts)   | message_id=1751234567.123456 isThreadReply=false reply_to_id=undefined
genuine reply (thread_ts!=ts) | message_id=1751234599.999999 isThreadReply=true reply_to_id="1751234567.123456"
```

Before the fix, `reply_to_id` equals `message_id` for both non-reply shapes; after the fix it is omitted, and the genuine reply still points at the parent message.

### 2. Regression tests

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

The new `replyToId gating` tests fail on `origin/main` and pass with this patch. `oxlint` on the changed files passes clean.
